title: No recording in Jackson; Little Brother Montgomery and Mister Walters
summary: Jackson had no recording equipment; local blues players like Little Brother Montgomery and Mister Walters went to Chicago to record.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: I don't know if they had any type of recording equipment around Jackson during that time. Because during that period, everybody had to go to Chicago to record. I remember the legendary Little Brother Montgomery used to play house parties at my house, and my grandfather played with him... He was Paul Gayten's uncle. And Little Brother...they used to have to go to Chicago to

record. And there was another fellow that my grandfather... Mister Walters. He used to go to Chicago, my grandfather and him, to make records. I think he's the guy that really made the first recording on the "How Long Blues"(?)/ "Howlin' Blues"(?) -- a guy named (?)Mister Walters(?)... Q: What was his name?
Mister Walters. I can't remember his first name. But he played the steel bodied guitar. You know, in those days, the blues players would sing the blues, and they...
...used to go to Chicago to make records. But there was no recording equipment in Jackson, down that far during that period. Q: [INAUDIBLE QUESTION]
